newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian zinc prices gain, copper and tin fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian zinc prices gain, copper and tin fall.

text.p: Indian zinc prices on Monday gained after a state producer raised its prices while copper and tin extended losses, dealers said.
Zinc rose by 100 rupees to 7,050 rupees per quintal on fresh speculative buying while arrivals were at low ebb, said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.
"State-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd has hiked selling prices by 2,500 rupees per tonne for the second half of the current month, while Hindustan Copper Ltd has kept prices unchanged," he said.
Copper fell by 50 rupees to 12,950 rupees per quintal on fresh offerings by the stockist following weak trends in the world market. Demand was dull.

Tin lost 100 rupees at 34,100 rupees per quintal on fresh arrivals. Nickel was steady at 37,200 rupees per quintal, aluminium at 7,250 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees in a narrow trading range on limited activity.
